transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A funny smell that remains after cleaning usually means there is still something decomposing in a hidden spot, or less commonly, an electrical component is overheating. First, please check if the smell resembles rotting food or burning plastic. If it smells like burning plastic, hot rubber, or smoke, stop using the fridge immediately and unplug it from the wall, as this indicates a serious electrical fault that requires a qualified engineer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Well, it's more like hot plastic, an electrical sort of smell, not rotten food. It's stronger round the back of the fridge. The plug feels a bit warm too, and I sometimes hear a buzzing from the back. Should I unplug it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, please unplug it immediately. Do not plug it back in or use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. The smell of hot plastic combined with warmth at the plug and buzzing from the rear strongly indicates an electrical fault—such as a failing start relay, damaged internal wiring, or a compressor issue—which is a fire hazard. Because this involves mains voltage and sealed components, it cannot be safely repaired by a homeowner. Please contact a qualified appliance engineer to diagnose and fix the electrical fault.

candidates: Spoilt food trapped in a hidden area (drain, drip tray, or seal) (high)
Electrical fault causing burning smell (safety critical) (medium)
plan: They asked: "Any ideas?" - answer that first.
Checks they have done and what they found: cleaned it out - smell is still there.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell in the kitchen". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
